complexity.notes: Each word's key is computed twice (once in the dict comprehension and again in the append loop); a single pass with collections.defaultdict(list) would be cleaner and avoid duplicate work. The return annotation 'tuple(int)' is not a valid type hint — use tuple[int, ...] from Python 3.9+. The keys are a bounded fixed-size signature, so lookups remain O(1) even in the worst case.
complexity.summary: Computes a 26-element character-count tuple as a canonical key for each word, groups words by that key in a dict, then returns the grouped values.
